newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Ex-Central African military leader's son arrested.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Central African military leader's son arrested.

text.p: The son of the Central African Republic's former military leader Andre Kolingba has been arrested following last weekend's army mutiny, sources among the mutineers said on Tuesday.
Major Guy Kolingba was detained on Monday after responding to a broadcast order to rejoin his command, the sources added, quoting witnesses. Loyalist army officers declined comment.

French troops and soldiers loyal to President Ange-Felix Patasse, who was on a visit to Europe, patrolled the centre of the capital Bangui on Tuesday. Residents said that traffic was slight, blaming a shortage of fuel and military checkpoints.

Soldiers in the Kassai Barracks on the outskirts of the city mutinied on Friday, following an attempt to arrest an officer who was a nephew of Andre Kolingba and was freed from jail during an army revolt put down by French troops in May.

Dissident soldiers, who also staged a pay revolt in April, on Saturday revived demands for back pay from 1992 and 1993 and for Patasse to revoke a decree ordering one of the regiments involved in the mutinies to a base away from the capital.
They also want recommendations of a national conference held after the May revolt implemented. These include creation of a professional army with a greater role in national life.

Kolingba, who assumed power in 1981 during the confusion that followed the ouster of self-styled emperor Jean-Bedel Bokassa two years earlier, introduced democratic reform but was among candidates Patasse defeated in a 1993 presidential poll.
